matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation and verify they are equal. Without this check you may accept a syntactically correct equation that is arithmetically false.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Once you have a candidate move that yields valid numeral and operator shapes, before finalizing compute the values of the left‑hand side and right‑hand side and ensure they match.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' without recomputing the side values, resulting in an equation that looks correct but does not satisfy the equality.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting glyph must correspond to a valid Roman numeral. Otherwise the character becomes an undefined shape such as a lone diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick move that involves a numeral, verify that both the source numeral (after losing a stick) and the destination numeral (after gaining a stick) are recognizable Roman numerals.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an 'X' and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator stick composition
matchstick.principle: Know the exact stick count and orientation for each allowed operator (+, -, =). Using the wrong number or orientation of sticks produces an invalid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick from or to an operator, check that the operator’s stick composition matches its definition.
matchstick.example: Constructing a '+' sign with two vertical sticks and one horizontal, which does not match the required one vertical plus one horizontal.

matchstick.title: Allowed operators only
matchstick.principle: The final equation may contain only '+', '-', and '=', and you must not introduce any other symbol. Introducing a non‑allowed operator makes the equation invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick move, scan the whole equation to ensure every operator is among the allowed set.
matchstick.example: Turning the '=' sign into a '≠' by adding a diagonal slash, which is not an allowed operator.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you cannot replace a vertical stick with a diagonal or rotate a stick during the move. Ignoring orientation creates impossible shapes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick, keep its original orientation; you may only relocate it, not re‑orient it.
matchstick.example: Replacing a vertical stick from an 'I' with a diagonal to form a 'V', which violates orientation constraints.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect only the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick). Changing more than two characters violates the puzzle rules.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a stick move, identify exactly which two characters will change and ensure no other character is altered.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from the '=' sign and also altering the '+' sign without moving a stick to it, thereby affecting three characters.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The final equation must contain exactly one '=' sign, which must remain the standard two‑horizontal‑stick form. Changing or removing the equality sign invalidates the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Never remove a horizontal stick from '=', unless you replace it with another stick to keep it as '=', and ensure there is exactly one '=' after the move.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from '=', leaving a single '-' sign and thus losing the equality operator.

matchstick.title: Operator source/destination validity
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from an operator, the source must remain a valid operator (+, -, =); when adding a stick to an operator, the resulting operator must be valid. Otherwise the operator becomes undefined.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During a stick move that involves operators, verify that both the operator you take a stick from and the operator you add a stick to stay valid after the move.
matchstick.example: Taking the vertical stick from '+' and leaving a '-' sign, but not adding that stick to another operator, resulting in an extra '-' and a missing stick.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick between numerals, consider known single‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X, L↔C) that keep both source and destination as valid Roman numerals. Ignoring these patterns can lead to invalid numerals or missed solutions.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If a stick move involves two numerals, check whether moving a stick can convert one into another valid numeral while the other also remains valid (e.g., moving a vertical stick from one I to another to turn I→II).
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from an 'X' to a 'V' and leaving the 'X' as a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral, instead of swapping the two so both stay valid.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: Provide the corrected equation as a single line prefixed with 'Correct version of the equation: ', with uppercase letters and whitespace collapsed. The scorer extracts the last such line, so any deviation causes a mismatch.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a valid corrected equation, output it exactly in the required format before submitting.
matchstick.example: Omitting the required prefix or adding extra spaces, causing the answer not to be recognized by the verifier.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often focuses on the visual stick move and forgets to check whether the resulting numbers satisfy the equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a move, compute the values of both sides and confirm they match before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When a stick is removed or added without considering the set of valid Roman‑numeral glyphs, the result can be a shape that does not correspond to any numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Validate the source and destination numerals after the move against the list of allowed Roman numerals.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may assemble operators with the wrong number or orientation of sticks, producing symbols that are not '+', '-', or '='.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recall the exact stick composition for each operator and check the operator after any stick transfer.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effectively removing a stick)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes a stick from a character without adding it elsewhere, violating the rule that exactly one stick must be relocated.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always identify both a source and a destination character for the stick; the move must transfer the stick, not delete it.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a stick from an operator can leave the source operator in an invalid form, or adding a stick can create a non‑allowed operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move involving operators, verify that both the source and destination operators remain within the allowed set.
